messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Whenever a book's cover changes, `Book::CoverProcessingJob` (in `app/jobs`)
is kicked off from the `Book` model and stamps the cover's SHA-256
fingerprint into the blob's metadata. In production it fails intermittently:
the worker picks it up before the database transaction that attached the
cover has committed, finds no file, and raises
`ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError`. Worse, when a save inside a larger
transaction is rolled back, the work for the never-committed cover is still
handed off — and errors on every retry. The search entry a book edit
refreshes goes the same way, off the same handover.

Fix when that background work is handed off. It should not be handed off
until the edit that kicked it off has committed, never while that edit is
still open — and if the edit is abandoned, it must never be handed off at
all.

The nightly importer runs the same edit over a whole batch, and applies the
batch all or nothing, so this has to hold there too. One thing must survive an
abandoned batch, though: the operator still hears that their import did not go
through. Losing that is how a failed import goes unnoticed until somebody asks.

On a successful edit the outcome is unchanged: the work still runs, the same
fingerprint is stamped and the search entry is refreshed. No new tables or
columns, and `bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it.

  def perform(book)

class Book < ApplicationRecord
  include Accessable, Editing, Sluggable

  has_many :leaves, dependent: :destroy
  has_one_attached :cover, dependent: :purge_later

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:title) }
  scope :published, -> { where(published: true) }

  enum :theme, %w[ black blue green magenta orange violet white ].index_by(&:itself), suffix: true, default: :blue

  def press(leafable, leaf_params)
    leaves.create! leaf_params.merge(leafable: leafable)
  end

  def markable
    leaves.active.positioned.map { it.leafable.markable }.join("\n\n")
  end
end

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end

module Book::Editing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def apply_edit(attributes)
    transaction do
      update!(attributes)
      Book::SearchIndexJob.perform_later(self)
      Book::CoverProcessingJob.set(wait: 5.seconds).perform_later(self) if attributes[:cover].present?
    end
  end
end

class Books::ImportsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    Book.transaction do
      book_batch.each do |id, attributes|
        Book.accessable_or_published.find(id).apply_edit(attributes)
      end
    rescue StandardError => error
      Books::ImportFailureJob.perform_later(Current.user.id, error.message)
      raise
    end

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def book_batch
      params.require(:books).each_pair.map do |id, attributes|
        [ id, attributes.permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover) ]
      end
    end

class Book::CoverProcessingJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(book)
    blob = book.cover.blob
    fingerprint = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(blob.download)
    blob.update!(metadata: blob.metadata.merge("sha256" => fingerprint))
  end
end

class Book < ApplicationRecord
  include Accessable, Editing, Sluggable

  has_many :leaves, dependent: :destroy
  has_one_attached :cover, dependent: :purge_later

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:title) }
  scope :published, -> { where(published: true) }

  enum :theme, %w[ black blue green magenta orange violet white ].index_by(&:itself), suffix: true, default: :blue

  def press(leafable, leaf_params)
    leaves.create! leaf_params.merge(leafable: leafable)
  end

  def markable
    leaves.active.positioned.map { it.leafable.markable }.join("\n\n")
  end
end

==> app/models/book/accessable.rb <==
module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end

module Book::Editing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def apply_edit(attributes)
    transaction do
      update!(attributes)
      Book::SearchIndexJob.perform_later(self)
      Book::CoverProcessingJob.set(wait: 5.seconds).perform_later(self) if attributes[:cover].present?
    end
  end
end

class Books::ImportsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    Book.transaction do
      book_batch.each do |id, attributes|
        Book.accessable_or_published.find(id).apply_edit(attributes)
      end
    rescue StandardError => error
      Books::ImportFailureJob.perform_later(Current.user.id, error.message)
      raise
    end

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def book_batch
      params.require(:books).each_pair.map do |id, attributes|
        [ id, attributes.permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover) ]
      end
    end
end

class BooksController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: %i[ index show ]

  before_action :ensure_index_is_not_empty, only: :index
  before_action :set_book, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]
  before_action :set_users, only: %i[ new edit ]
  before_action :ensure_editable, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @books = Book.accessable_or_published.ordered
  end

  def new
    @book = Book.new
  end

  def create
    book = Book.create! book_params
    update_accesses(book)

    redirect_to book_slug_url(book)
  end

  def show
    @leaves = @book.leaves.active.with_leafables.positioned

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @book.apply_edit(book_params)
    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

    def ensure_index_is_not_empty
      if !signed_in? && Book.published.none?
        require_authentication
      end
    end

    def book_params
      params.require(:book).permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover, :remove_cover, :everyone_access, :theme)
    end

    def update_accesses(book)
      editors = [ Current.user.id, *params[:editor_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]
      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

      book.update_access(editors: editors, readers: readers)
    end

    def remove_cover
      @book.cover.purge
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into a Tricky Rails Conundrum**

Okay, here's what's running through my mind. This problem is classic: a race condition between a database transaction and a background job in Rails, exacerbated by potential transaction rollbacks and batch processing. My expert brain is already dissecting the specifics.

First, let's break down the core issue. A cover change triggers `Book::CoverProcessingJob`, which calculates the SHA-256 fingerprint and saves it to the blob's metadata. The intermittent failures in production – `ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError` – are a huge red flag. The worker is picking up the job *before* the database transaction attaching the cover has fully committed. That means the file isn't there, and boom – error. And even worse, when a save is rolled back, the work for a cover that never actually got committed is *still* handed off, leading to repeated errors on retry.

The prompt is crystal clear about the desired fix. The background work *must not* be handed off until the initiating edit/transaction has committed. If the edit is abandoned, the job should *never* run. This is crucial for both single edits and the nightly importer batch processes. The importer is a slightly different beast, but the core principle applies. If a batch fails, we need to ensure the operator is aware, without running potentially thousands of failed jobs. However, if everything runs smoothly, there should be no changes to the successful outcome, and the tests must pass. No new tables, no new columns. I love those constraints!

Now, my mind is racing through potential solutions. I'm thinking of Rails's transaction management features. `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` and `ActiveJob::EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit` are the obvious starting points. I'm also considering `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`. The Resque adapter is in the picture too, so I need to understand how it behaves in this context. I'm going to start digging into the Rails source code itself. I'll need to examine `ActiveJob::EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit`, `ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::ResqueAdapter`, the `TestAdapter` (crucial for testing the fix!), `ActiveJob::Base`, `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`, `config.load_defaults`, and `ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob`. The devil, as always, is in the details. Time to start the deep inspection!

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "resque"
require "active_support/core_ext/enumerable"
require "active_support/core_ext/array/access"

begin
  require "resque-scheduler"
rescue LoadError
  begin
    require "resque_scheduler"
  rescue LoadError
    false
  end
end

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Resque adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Resque (pronounced like "rescue") is a Redis-backed library for creating
    # background jobs, placing those jobs on multiple queues, and processing
    # them later.
    #
    # Read more about Resque {here}[https://github.com/resque/resque].
    #
    # To use Resque set the queue_adapter config to +:resque+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :resque
    class ResqueAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        JobWrapper.instance_variable_set(:@queue, job.queue_name)
        Resque.enqueue_to job.queue_name, JobWrapper, job.serialize
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        unless Resque.respond_to?(:enqueue_at_with_queue)
          raise NotImplementedError, "To be able to schedule jobs with Resque you need the " \
            "resque-scheduler gem. Please add it to your Gemfile and run bundle install"
        end
        Resque.enqueue_at_with_queue job.queue_name, timestamp, JobWrapper, job.serialize
      end

      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        class << self
          def perform(job_data)
            Base.execute job_data
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Test adapter for Active Job
    #
    # The test adapter should be used only in testing. Along with
    # ActiveJob::TestCase and ActiveJob::TestHelper
    # it makes a great tool to test your \Rails application.
    #
    # To use the test adapter set +queue_adapter+ config to +:test+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :test
    class TestAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      attr_accessor(:perform_enqueued_jobs, :perform_enqueued_at_jobs, :filter, :reject, :queue, :at, :stopping)
      attr_writer(:enqueued_jobs, :performed_jobs)

      # Provides a store of all the enqueued jobs with the TestAdapter so you can check them.
      def enqueued_jobs
        @enqueued_jobs ||= []
      end

      # Provides a store of all the performed jobs with the TestAdapter so you can check them.
      def performed_jobs
        @performed_jobs ||= []
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job_data = job_to_hash(job)
        perform_or_enqueue(perform_enqueued_jobs && !filtered?(job), job, job_data)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job_data = job_to_hash(job, at: timestamp)
        perform_or_enqueue(perform_enqueued_at_jobs && !filtered?(job), job, job_data)
      end

      def stopping?
        @stopping.is_a?(Proc) ? @stopping.call : @stopping
      end

      private
        def job_to_hash(job, extras = {})
          job.serialize.tap do |job_data|
            job_data[:job] = job.class
            job_data[:args] = job_data.fetch("arguments")
            job_data[:queue] = job_data.fetch("queue_name")
            job_data[:priority] = job_data.fetch("priority")
          end.merge(extras)
        end

        def perform_or_enqueue(perform, job, job_data)
          if perform
            performed_jobs << job_data
            Base.execute(job.serialize)
          else
            enqueued_jobs << job_data
          end
        end

        def filtered?(job)
          filtered_queue?(job) || filtered_job_class?(job) || filtered_time?(job)
        end

        def filtered_time?(job)
          job.scheduled_at > at if at && job.scheduled_at
        end

        def filtered_queue?(job)
          if queue
            job.queue_name != queue.to_s
          end
        end

        def filtered_job_class?(job)
          if filter
            !filter_as_proc(filter).call(job)
          elsif reject
            filter_as_proc(reject).call(job)
          end
        end

        def filter_as_proc(filter)
          return filter if filter.is_a?(Proc)

          ->(job) { Array(filter).include?(job.class) }
        end
    end
  end
end

**A Moment of Clarity and Rigorous Dissection**

Whoa, this is incredibly clear now! The system's architecture and the potential failure points are laid bare. Let's meticulously dissect every detail.

My immediate focus is on ensuring that background jobs related to book updates are *not* enqueued until the database transaction that initiated them has successfully committed. The current implementation in `app/models/book/editing.rb` is vulnerable, and I'm starting to see why, particularly in relation to the `Book::CoverProcessingJob`, and the importer controller!

I'm zeroing in on the implications of `config.active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true`, which is the likely cause of the intermittent failures in production, as well as the silent failure of the import job! In the import controller (`Books::ImportsController`), the use of `Book.transaction do ... end` combined with the `rescue StandardError => error` block creates a critical race condition when combined with deferred job enqueuing.

The fact that the rescue block is *inside* the transaction is the key.  If a book update fails within the batch, the rescue block attempts to enqueue `Books::ImportFailureJob` *before* the transaction is rolled back.  If `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` is enabled, this job will also be deferred, and thus silently discarded when the entire transaction rolls back! This is exactly what the prompt highlighted. The operator is not notified, and a failed import remains unnoticed.

Now, let's turn to the potential impact of `.set(wait: 5.seconds)` on the `Book::CoverProcessingJob`. This introduces a delay, potentially exacerbating the race condition between the database commit and the job's execution if `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` is enabled. If the transaction *does* roll back, and the job is enqueued with the transaction deferred, the file won't exist.

My strategy is taking shape: Ensure that jobs are *only* enqueued *after* the database transaction commits.  We need to look at whether we should modify `Book::Editing`, or the controllers, or the jobs themselves to achieve that.

module ActiveJob
  # Provides behavior for enqueuing jobs.

  # Can be raised by adapters if they wish to communicate to the caller a reason
  # why the adapter was unexpectedly unable to enqueue a job.
  class EnqueueError < StandardError; end

  class << self
    # Push many jobs onto the queue at once without running enqueue callbacks.
    # Queue adapters may communicate the enqueue status of each job by setting
    # successfully_enqueued and/or enqueue_error on the passed-in job instances.
    def perform_all_later(*jobs)
      jobs.flatten!
      jobs.group_by(&:queue_adapter).each do |queue_adapter, adapter_jobs|
        instrument_enqueue_all(queue_adapter, adapter_jobs) do
          if queue_adapter.respond_to?(:enqueue_all)
            queue_adapter.enqueue_all(adapter_jobs)
          else
            adapter_jobs.each do |job|
              job.successfully_enqueued = false
              if job.scheduled_at
                queue_adapter.enqueue_at(job, job.scheduled_at.to_f)
              else
                queue_adapter.enqueue(job)
              end
              job.successfully_enqueued = true
            rescue EnqueueError => e
              job.enqueue_error = e
            end
            adapter_jobs.count(&:successfully_enqueued?)
          end
        end
      end
      nil
    end
  end

  module Enqueuing
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      ##
      # :singleton-method:
      #
      # Defines if enqueueing this job from inside an Active Record transaction
      # automatically defers the enqueue to after the transaction commits.
      #
      # It can be set on a per job basis:
      #  - true forces the job to be deferred.
      #  - false forces the job to be queued immediately.
      class_attribute :enqueue_after_transaction_commit, instance_accessor: false, instance_predicate: false, default: false
    end

    # Includes the +perform_later+ method for job initialization.
    module ClassMethods
      # Push a job onto the queue. By default the arguments must be either String,
      # Integer, Float, NilClass, TrueClass, FalseClass, BigDecimal, Symbol, Date,
      # Time, DateTime, ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, ActiveSupport::Duration,
      # Hash, ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess, Array, Range, or
      # GlobalID::Identification instances, although this can be extended by adding
      # custom serializers.
      #
      # Returns an instance of the job class queued with arguments available in
      # Job#arguments or +false+ if the enqueue did not succeed.
      #
      # After the attempted enqueue, the job will be yielded to an optional block.
      #
      # If Active Job is used conjointly with Active Record, and #perform_later is called
      # inside an Active Record transaction, then the enqueue is implicitly deferred to after
      # the transaction is committed, or dropped if it's rolled back. In such case #perform_later
      # will return the job instance like if it was successfully enqueued, but will still return
      # +false+ if a callback prevented the job from being enqueued.
      #
      # This behavior can be changed on a per job basis:
      #
      #  class NotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      #    self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false
      #  end
      def perform_later(...)
        job = job_or_instantiate(...)
        enqueue_result = job.enqueue

        yield job if block_given?

        enqueue_result
      end

      private
        def job_or_instantiate(*args, &) # :doc:
          args.first.is_a?(self) ? args.first : new(*args)
        end
        ruby2_keywords(:job_or_instantiate)
    end

    # Enqueues the job to be performed by the queue adapter.
    #
    # ==== Options
    # * <tt>:wait</tt> - Enqueues the job with the specified delay
    # * <tt>:wait_until</tt> - Enqueues the job at the time specified
    # * <tt>:queue</tt> - Enqueues the job on the specified queue
    # * <tt>:priority</tt> - Enqueues the job with the specified priority
    #
    # ==== Examples
    #
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue wait: 5.minutes
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue queue: :important
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue wait_until: Date.tomorrow.midnight
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue priority: 10
    def enqueue(options = {})
      set(options)
      self.successfully_enqueued = false

      raw_enqueue

      if successfully_enqueued?
        self
      else
        false
      end
    end

    private
      def raw_enqueue
        run_callbacks :enqueue do
          _raw_enqueue
        end
      end

      def _raw_enqueue
        if scheduled_at
          queue_adapter.enqueue_at self, scheduled_at.to_f
        else
          queue_adapter.enqueue self
        end

        self.successfully_enqueued = true
      rescue EnqueueError => e
        self.enqueue_error = e
      end
  end
end

**Analyzing the Root Cause of the Intermittent Job Failure**

Okay, deep breath. I need to figure out why this `Book::CoverProcessingJob` is failing intermittently in production. The issue, as I understand it, is that the worker is picking up the job before the database transaction that attaches the cover has committed. This is leading to `ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError`. Furthermore, even if a save is rolled back, the work for the never-committed cover is still handed off, causing errors on every retry. And, critically, this applies to the search index refresh too.

First, I need to understand the role of `.set(wait: 5.seconds)`. Why was it added to `Book::CoverProcessingJob`? Was it a naive attempt at a fix, a band-aid to address this race condition (hoping that 5 seconds would give the database transaction enough time to complete), or something more intentional? Maybe the timer was specifically put there so `Book::CoverProcessingJob` utilizes `ConfiguredJob`, or perhaps someone was using `ResqueAdapter` and checking the `perform_enqueued_jobs` option. I *must* test and understand both possibilities!

I'm starting to get a better handle on the potential problem. My current hypothesis is that the `.set(wait: 5.seconds)` was added in an attempt to address the race condition. With `.set(wait: 5.seconds)` the assumption is, or was, that 5 seconds would be enough time for the database transaction to commit, and the file to be available.

    # = Active Job Async adapter

    #     idletime: 600.seconds
    #
    # The adapter uses a {Concurrent Ruby}[https://github.com/ruby-concurrency/concurrent-ruby] thread pool to schedule and execute
    # jobs. Since jobs share a single thread pool, long-running jobs will block
    # short-lived jobs. Fine for dev/test; bad for production.

      # See {Concurrent::ThreadPoolExecutor}[https://ruby-concurrency.github.io/concurrent-ruby/master/Concurrent/ThreadPoolExecutor.html] for executor options.
      def initialize(**executor_options)

      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        @scheduler.enqueue JobWrapper.new(job), queue_name: job.queue_name
      end

      # any new jobs following the executor's fallback policy (`caller_runs`).
      # Waits for termination by default. Pass `wait: false` to continue.

      end

      # Used for our test suite.
      def immediate=(immediate) # :nodoc:
        @scheduler.immediate = immediate
      end

      # Note that we don't actually need to serialize the jobs since we're
      # performing them in-process, but we do so anyway for parity with other
      # adapters and deployment environments. Otherwise, serialization bugs
      # may creep in undetected.
      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        def initialize(job)
          job.provider_job_id = SecureRandom.uuid
          @job_data = job.serialize
        end

        def perform

        end
      end

      class Scheduler # :nodoc:
        DEFAULT_EXECUTOR_OPTIONS = {
          min_threads:     0,
          max_threads:     ENV.fetch("RAILS_MAX_THREADS", 5).to_i,
          auto_terminate:  true,
          idletime:        60, # 1 minute

          fallback_policy: :caller_runs # shouldn't matter -- 0 max queue
        }.freeze

          @immediate_executor = Concurrent::ImmediateExecutor.new

          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

          "/u/" + attachment.slug
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def localize_ref_links(page, pages)
        re = %r{
          (\[.+\])              # link title
          \(                    # opening paren
          \/\d+\/[\w-]+\/\d+\/  # leading portion of path
          ([\w-]+)              # leaf slug
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          link_title, leaf_slug, anchor = $1, $2, $3
          linked_page = pages[leaf_slug]
          raise "Invalid reference link: #{page_title}" unless linked_page.present?

          url = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.leafable_slug_path(linked_page.leaf, anchor: anchor, only_path: true)

          "#{link_title}(#{url}"
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def with_attachment(filename)
        File.open(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/#{filename}")) do |file|
          yield io: file, filename: filename
        end
      end
  end
end

    Book.transaction do
      upload = Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(file_path, "image/webp")
      book.apply_edit(title: "Real Tx Rollback", cover: upload)
      assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::SearchIndexJob
      assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::CoverProcessingJob

    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::SearchIndexJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::CoverProcessingJob
    assert_equal "Real Tx Book", book.reload.title

      upload = Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(file_path, "image/webp")
      book.apply_edit(title: "Real Tx Commit", cover: upload)
    end
    assert_equal "Real Tx Commit", book.reload.title
    assert_equal expected_sha, book.cover.blob.metadata["sha256"]
    assert_equal "Real Tx Commit", Rails.cache.read("search_index/book/#{book.id}")
  ensure
    book&.destroy!
    Rails.cache = original_cache
  end
end

    Rails.cache = ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore.new
    sign_in :kevin
  end

  teardown do
    Rails.cache = @original_cache
  end

  test "abandoned batch via JSON NotNullViolation drops book jobs and enqueues ImportFailureJob" do
    books(:manual).update!(published: true)
    handbook = books(:handbook)
    manual = books(:manual)
    original_title = handbook.title

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation) do
      post books_import_path, params: {
        books: {
          handbook.id => { title: "Should Rollback" },
          manual.id => { title: nil }
        }
      }, as: :json
    end

    assert_equal original_title, handbook.reload.title
    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::SearchIndexJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::CoverProcessingJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Books::ImportFailureJob

    perform_enqueued_jobs
    assert_not_nil Rails.cache.read("import_failure/#{users(:kevin).id}")
    assert_nil Rails.cache.read("search_index/book/#{handbook.id}")
  end

  test "abandoned batch with cover on book 1 and unexpected StandardError on book 2" do
    books(:manual).update!(published: true)
    handbook = books(:handbook)
    manual = books(:manual)
    original_title = handbook.title
    upload = fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")

    # Raise on second book's apply_edit
    original_apply_edit = Book.instance_method(:apply_edit)
    Book.define_method(:apply_edit) do |attrs|
      raise "import boom" if id == manual.id
      original_apply_edit.bind_call(self, attrs)
    end

    begin
      err = assert_raises(RuntimeError) do
        post books_import_path, params: {
          books: {
            handbook.id => { title: "Should Rollback", cover: upload },
            manual.id => { title: "Boom" }
          }
        }
      end
      assert_equal "import boom", err.message
    ensure
      Book.define_method(:apply_edit, original_apply_edit)
    end

    assert_equal original_title, handbook.reload.title
    assert_not handbook.cover.attached?
    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::SearchIndexJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::CoverProcessingJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Books::ImportFailureJob
    assert_enqueued_with(job: Books::ImportFailureJob, args: [users(:kevin).id, "import boom"])
  end

  test "during batch import, jobs are not enqueued while transaction is open between book 1 and book 2" do
    books(:manual).update!(published: true)
    handbook = books(:handbook)
    manual = books(:manual)
    upload = fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")
    enqueued_mid_batch = nil

    original_apply_edit = Book.instance_method(:apply_edit)
    Book.define_method(:apply_edit) do |attrs|
      if id == manual.id
        enqueued_mid_batch = ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter.enqueued_jobs.dup
      end
      original_apply_edit.bind_call(self, attrs)
    end

    begin
      post books_import_path, params: {
        books: {
          handbook.id => { title: "Book 1", cover: upload },
          manual.id => { title: "Book 2" }
        }
      }
    ensure
      Book.define_method(:apply_edit, original_apply_edit)
    end

    assert_redirected_to root_url
    assert_equal [], enqueued_mid_batch, "No jobs should be enqueued mid-batch before commit!"
    assert_enqueued_jobs 2, only: Book::SearchIndexJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Book::CoverProcessingJob
  end

  test "ActiveJob.perform_all_later respects enqueue_after_transaction_commit per job" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    Book.transaction do
      ActiveJob.perform_all_later(
        Book::SearchIndexJob.new(book),
        Book::CoverProcessingJob.new(book),
        Books::ImportFailureJob.new(users(:kevin).id, "immediate")
      )
      assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::SearchIndexJob
      assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::CoverProcessingJob
      assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Books::ImportFailureJob
      raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
    end

    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::SearchIndexJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 0, only: Book::CoverProcessingJob
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Books::ImportFailureJob
  end
end
EOF
